MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the total value of the digit 5 in 7,250? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 50
   C. 500
   D. 5

2. Round 342 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 330
   B. 300
   C. 350
   D. 340

3. Which list shows all the factors of 18? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18
   B. 1, 2, 6, 9, 18
   C. 1, 2, 3, 6, 9
   D. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 18

4. Work out 1,856 + 4,567. (1 mark)
   A. 6,323
   B. 6,433
   C. 6,423
   D. 5,313

5. Work out 2,450 + 3,875. (1 mark)
   A. 6,325
   B. 6,225
   C. 5,225
   D. 6,335

6. A trader saved Ksh 4,650 in the first term and Ksh 2,875 in the second term. How much did she save? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 7,625
   B. Ksh 6,425
   C. Ksh 7,515
   D. Ksh 7,525

7. Work out 6,003 − 2,475. (1 mark)
   A. 3,528
   B. 3,538
   C. 3,428
   D. 4,472

8. Estimate 9,317 − 4,582 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 4,750
   B. 4,740
   C. 4,840
   D. 4,730

9. Work out 7,300 − 4,562. (1 mark)
   A. 2,638
   B. 2,748
   C. 2,738
   D. 3,262

10. What is 12 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 12,000
   B. 120
   C. 1,200
   D. 112

11. What is 52 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 82
   B. 1,560
   C. 15,600
   D. 156

12. What is 34 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 134
   B. 340
   C. 34,000
   D. 3,400

13. 38 mangoes are shared equally among 5 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 7
   C. 2
   D. 3

14. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 8 × 3 = 24? (1 mark)
   A. 3 ÷ 8 = 24
   B. 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   C. 24 ÷ 24 = 8
   D. 24 ÷ 8 = 8

15. A rectangle is cut into 5 equal parts and 2 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 2/3
   B. 2/5
   C. 3/5
   D. 5/2

16. A circle is cut into 10 equal parts and 7 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 3/7
   B. 10/3
   C. 7/10
   D. 3/10

17. Change 4 3/8 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 7/8
   B. 35/8
   C. 36/8
   D. 32/8

18. A hundred square has 5 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.005
   B. 5
   C. 0.5
   D. 0.05

19. In the number 4.05, the digit 5 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tenths
   C. Hundredths
   D. Tens

20. Write 7/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.7
   B. 0.07
   C. 7.0
   D. 0.17

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A farmer has 95 eggs to pack into trays that each hold 6 eggs. (a) How many full trays are there and how many eggs are left over? (b) How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (5 marks)

22. Find 3/4 of 12 counters. Explain each step. (3 marks)

23. Ksh 3.50 is given as 3 shillings and 50 cents. Write 75 cents and 5 cents as decimals of a shilling. (3 marks)

24. A class has 30 pupils. Two fifths of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school? (3 marks)

25. Complete the pattern 3, 6, 12, 24, ... with the next two numbers and state the rule. (3 marks)

26. Njoki has 9 halves of oranges. How many whole oranges is that? Write your answer as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

27. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction and then change your answer back to an improper fraction to check it. (4 marks)

28. Work out 34 × 100 and 60 × 100. (2 marks)

29. Wangari buys 24 exercise books at Ksh 18 each. Estimate the total cost by rounding to the nearest ten, then work out the exact cost. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 50
   The digit 5 is in the tens place, so its total value is 5 × 10 = 50.

2. D — 340
   Look at the ones digit 2. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 342 rounds to 340.

3. A — 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 18. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.

4. C — 6,423
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 1,856 + 4,567 = 6,423.

5. A — 6,325
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 2,450 + 3,875 = 6,325.

6. D — Ksh 7,525
   Add 4,650 + 2,875 = 7,525 Ksh.

7. A — 3,528
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 6,003 − 2,475 = 3,528. Check: 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003.

8. B — 4,740
   9,317 rounds to 9,320 and 4,582 rounds to 4,580. 9,320 − 4,580 = 4,740.

9. C — 2,738
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 7,300 − 4,562 = 2,738. Check: 2,738 + 4,562 = 7,300.

10. C — 1,200
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 12 × 100 = 1,200.

11. B — 1,560
   52 × 3 = 156, then × 10 gives 1,560.

12. D — 3,400
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 34 × 100 = 3,400.

13. D — 3
   38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. Each child gets 7 and 3 are left.

14. B — 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 8 × 3 = 24, we know 24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

15. B — 2/5
   The whole has 5 equal parts and 2 are shaded, so 2/5 is shaded.

16. D — 3/10
   Not shaded: 10 − 7 = 3 parts, so 3/10.

17. B — 35/8
   4 × 8 = 32 and 32 + 3 = 35. The denominator stays 8, so the answer is 35/8.

18. D — 0.05
   5 out of 100 squares is 5/100 = 0.05.

19. C — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 4.05 the digit 5 is in the hundredths place.

20. A — 0.7
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 7/10 = 0.7.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 15 full trays and 5 eggs left over (b) 16 trays
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 95 ÷ 6 = 15 remainder 5, 1 mark for stating both, 1 mark for the leftover eggs needing another tray, 1 mark for 16.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 counters. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 counters in one quarter; 3 × 3 = 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by the denominator, 1 mark for multiplying by the numerator, 1 mark for the answer.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.75 and 0.05 of a shilling (Ksh 0.75 and Ksh 0.05)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the idea that 100 cents = 1 shilling, 1 mark for each decimal.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 12 pupils
   Working / marking points: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 (1 mark); 6 × 2 = 12 (1 mark); answer with unit (1 mark).

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: multiply by 2. Next numbers: 48 and 96.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule, 1 mark for each correct number.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/2 oranges
   Working / marking points: 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1 (2 marks); 4 1/2 (1 mark).

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: 11/4 = 2 3/4. Check: 2 × 4 = 8 and 8 + 3 = 11, so 11/4.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 3/4 with working, 2 marks for the correct check.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3,400 and 6,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each. Move each digit two places left.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 20 × 20 = 400. Exact: 24 × 18 = 432 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 400, 1 mark for the exact working (24 × 8 = 192 and 24 × 10 = 240), 1 mark for 432.
